api: run_measured_anonymous(argv, cwd, fds, *, stdin_fd=None, **guard_options) -> (guard_record, bounded_stdout, raw_child_observation)
architecture: The caller retains the existing serial verification lease. The wrapper forwards every guard option unchanged to existing run_anonymous; no guard, driver, acceptance or production file is changed.

The parent copies the static wrapper Python source into a sealed memfd and allocates a fresh report memfd. Existing guard descriptor reopening and token expansion transport both without named generated files.

Inside the existing scope, a fresh wrapper launches exactly one target child. It preserves cwd, environment, session, process group and inherited rlimits; the existing outer worker still disables core files.
os.wait4(process.pid, 0) reaps that exact child and returns its kernel resource record. It does not use cumulative getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) or statistics from the outer systemd launcher.

Only original payload descriptors are inherited by the target. Wrapper source/report descriptors close on target exec. Stdin is /dev/null unless an existing payload memfd is selected; target stdout/stderr retain the guard routing and bounds.
A bounded numeric report is written once into its separate memfd, then sealed. The target output stream is not altered by measurement JSON.

Normal target exit codes are returned unchanged. Natural target signals are explicitly recorded and re-raised by the wrapper; existing guard-worker mapping to128+signal remains intact. Cancellation can produce a missing report and is never treated as a successful observation.

Parent-side parsing checks nonce, sealed bounded record, numeric types and consistency of raw wait status, code and signal. It retains raw failed observations but grants no semantic, resource-scaling or optimization admission.

caller_obligations: Continue binding the exact executable/production receipt, workload/profile/cell/revision and guard evidence using the future frozen Q01 resource contract.
Record absolute scope/allocator metrics separately and preserve failed/inconclusive samples.
Use identical wrapper/configuration and sufficient target CPU signal for paired comparisons.
metric_contract.cpu: user_cpu_seconds and system_cpu_seconds from the selected wait4 rusage record; entire target lifetime including fork/exec/startup/setup and kernel-attributed waited descendants.
metric_contract.failure: Guard stop, overflow, incomplete cleanup, missing/malformed report or changed source binding prevents raw-observation completion. Natural nonzero target exits can retain raw numeric observations but do not grant any acceptance.
metric_contract.rss: Absolute Linux ru_maxrss KiB and bytes (KiB*1024). This is a kernel lifetime high-water observation, not aggregate concurrent cgroup RSS, not a target-interval delta, and not a MiniKQL allocation counter.
metric_contract.wrapper_overhead: Wrapper-parent CPU is excluded by exact-child wait4; child pre-exec/startup overhead remains. Existing scope watchdog accounts the extra wrapper process, and all original ceilings stay unchanged.

primary_references.fact: Positive-pid wait4 selects the specific child and supplies its resource usage.
Linux ru_maxrss units are KiB; child accounting has descendant/largest-child limitations, and CPU values describe user/system execution.
Python exposes the waited pid, raw status and resource structure; waitstatus_to_exitcode preserves the distinction between exit and signal.

priority: Future Q01 resource work after correctness; not a prerequisite for C31/C47.
unresolved_before_use: Independent source review of descriptor ownership, signal propagation and cancelled-child cleanup is still required.

No process was launched and no rusage observation was collected. Future guarded integration must verify normal/nonzero/signal exits, failed exec, cancellation/timeout/memory stops, stdout overflow and cleanup without relaxing any guard.
Future descriptor checks must verify stdin payload transport, unchanged target stdout/stderr, report/source descriptors excluded from target inheritance and no generated disk output.

Future resource checks must verify sequential fresh calls do not share accounting, named units agree with Linux kernel observations, and the Python/fork startup floor does not dominate accepted samples.
No Q01 acceptance interface, scaling threshold, matrix runner or performance assertion is enabled by this module.
The wrapper supplies whole-child observations only; operator-only CPU and MiniKQL allocation/peak interval instrumentation remain separate work.
